label: test-name-tag-output-conventions
name: A test's name, tag or log output states the opposite of its assertions or breaks the file's convention
description: What breaks: the test misleads. SECTION still named 'append_v preserves poison' while it asserts the poison is zeroed (4188336324, check 5 as written); a TEST_CASE tagged '[hwattention][pos]' where every sibling carries one tag equal to its name (2828707534 'is/was the intention to start grouping ...?'); a mismatch count printed unconditionally where siblings print only when nonzero (2620236334 'Should be consistent?'). Procedure: run check 5 on names; compare each new TEST_CASE's tag list with the file's pattern; compare unconditional spdlog::info of a result with the sibling units' guards.
disposition_reason: Check 5 covers the name's verb; tags and output guards are the same 'match the file's convention' reading applied to the test's other labels.
agent_feasibility: yes: all three are static comparisons within the test file.

members.concern: The SECTION is still named 'append_v preserves poison' but its assertions now check that the poison (a NaN written on purpose into an unused slot) is zeroed, so the name states the opposite of what the test enforces.

detection.trigger: The diff rewrites an assertion, a comment or the stimulus inside a TEST_CASE/SECTION whose name is unchanged, or a comment inside the unit flips a verb to its opposite (preserve/zero, keep/drop) while the name keeps the old verb.
detection.procedure: extract the verb and object from the SECTION name; read the setup lines and every REQUIRE on the object; write 'fails when <state>' for each; compare the passing state with the name's verb and with the verb the unit's own new comments use; grep the name in the file header comment and the PR body for rename sites.
detection.question: Reading the name, the setup and the REQUIRE lines, does the name's verb describe the state in which the assertions pass?

members.quote: Nit: the section is still named "append_v preserves poison", but it now asserts that the poison is zeroed.
members.note: Anchored at t/t_llama_unit.cpp:3293 (96a6220ab6), TEST_CASE 'scaled_v padding NaN' [kv_data]. The hunk's new comment says the last copy lands 'next to the poisoned token 7' and the assertions require the partner to be zero. Renamed at c5d44bd86f to 'append_v zeroes the poisoned partner', with the file comment above the case updated.

members.concern: The new Catch2 TEST_CASE 'polymorphic cacheblock xfer' is tagged '[hwattention][pos]' while every other test in the file carries one tag equal to its own name; Wade suggests '[poly_cacheblock_xfer]' and asks whether grouping under '[hwattention]' was intended, noting it is the only test with that tag.

detection.trigger: A new TEST_CASE or TEST_CASE_METHOD has a tag list whose pattern differs from the other test units in the same file (different tag count, a tag no sibling uses, or a tag not derived from the test name).
detection.procedure: grep -n 'TEST_CASE' t/<file> at HEAD; tabulate (name, tags) per unit; count members per tag. A tag with exactly one member that no sibling uses, in a file where siblings follow one convention, is a candidate. Also note whether the new unit uses TEST_CASE while siblings use TEST_CASE_METHOD(fixture, ...). Offer the convention-conforming tag as a suggestion block and ask whether the new grouping is deliberate.
detection.question: Does the new test's tag follow the file's existing convention, and if not, is the new grouping deliberate and applied to the sibling tests?

members.quote: maybe? Or... is/was the intention to start grouping a subset of these tests under the `[hwattention]` category (which makes sense too)? It's just that this is the only test using that atm...
members.note: Verified at 9d64b4a8bf: t/t_hwattention.cpp has 13 test units; 11 are TEST_CASE_METHOD(fixture, "<name>", "[<name>]"); the new one at line 1787 is a plain TEST_CASE with '[hwattention][pos]'; 'dma_xfer_state comparison' at 1869 is also a plain TEST_CASE with '[dma_xfer_state]'. At the final head f0134b976b line 1789 reads TEST_CASE("polymorphic hwcacheblock xfer", "[poly_hwcacheblock_xfer]") - author renamed both the test and the tag. Check 5 (test name states the enforced contract) shares the theme of test naming but its trigger (assertion/comment change versus name verb) does not fire on a tag-only mismatch; fit none.

members.concern: The new test prints the overall mismatch count unconditionally at info level, while the older tests in the same file print their mismatch count only when it is nonzero; he offers a suggestion block adding 'if (k_mm || v_mm)' and asks for consistency.

detection.trigger: A new TEST_CASE in an existing test file adds an unconditional spdlog::info/warn/error call that reports a count or result that the REQUIRE on the next line already checks, while sibling TEST_CASEs in the same file guard the equivalent print with 'if (count > 0)' or 'if (count)'.
detection.procedure: In the test file at HEAD, grep -n 'mismatch' (or the counter name) and read each print site with 3 lines of context. Record for each sibling whether the print is guarded. If the new unit differs from the file's pattern, propose the guard as a suggestion block. Also check the log level matches the siblings (error vs info).
detection.question: Does every other unit in this file print this kind of result only when it is nonzero, and does the new one print it always?

members.quote: ... in the other tests, this is only printed if there were actually mismatches found. Should be consistent?
members.note: Verified sibling pattern at c5fd3de93b t/t_hwattention.cpp:566-568: 'if (mismatch_count > 0) { spdlog::error("K validation found {} mismatches", mismatch_count); }' then REQUIRE(mismatch_count == 0); same at :597, :714, :744 (all spdlog::error, guarded). The head c5fd3de93b already contains his suggestion verbatim at :1376-1377, including its two-space-less indentation ('if (k_mm || v_mm)' at column 0), which matches the commit subject 'Update t/t_hwattention.cpp' (a committed suggestion). He did not point out that the siblings use spdlog::error while the new line keeps spdlog::info. The per-fetcher print at :1367-1368 stayed unconditional; he did not flag it.

codex_bullets.bullet: Keep test names, setup, comments, and passing assertions consistent. Fix an invalid test fixture instead of adding production guards that silently hide bad state.
codex_bullets.reason: Four comments (PRs 4557, 4596, 2078, 1666). The second sentence (4125033677) is a distinct rule the Claude skill lacks; see also C26.
codex_bullets.claude_skill_coverage: partial (check 5 covers the name; the fixture-vs-production-guard sentence has no check)
